extracted.intended_audience: telecom industry participants, regulatory/compliance counsel, service providers, and policy stakeholders monitoring FCC robocall/caller ID authentication rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and evaluate stakeholder positions and procedural milestones in the FCC rulemaking on caller ID authentication and robocall mitigation, including proposals to transition to all-IP networks, STIR/SHAKEN implementation, and non‑IP authentication alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: All‑IP upgrade and STIR/SHAKEN implementation or non‑IP alternatives (NPRM requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking proposes requiring voice service providers to either upgrade their networks to all‑IP and implement STIR/SHAKEN or implement one or more of the three non‑IP call authentication standards proposed in the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core regulatory proposal framing operators' compliance choices: either complete an IP migration and deploy STIR/SHAKEN or adopt one (or more) of the FCC's identified non‑IP authentication frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize facilitating transition to all‑IP networks over mandating specific non‑IP solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple industry groups argued that, rather than mandating specific, non‑IP caller ID authentication solutions, the FCC should prioritize facilitating the transition to all IP‑based networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments suggest the FCC should use policy tools (deadlines, incentives, industry coordination) to speed IP migration instead of imposing divergent non‑IP mandates that could divert resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an industry working group to guide IP transition (NCTA recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCTA recommended that the FCC establish an industry working group to guide the final stages of an IP transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A working group is proposed as a collaborative mechanism to resolve final technical/interoperability issues and coordinate industry timelines for migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess non‑IP solution availability and effectiveness under TRACED Act standards
rubrics_metrics.description: USTelecom expressed skepticism that the FCC's proposed non‑IP authentication solutions have the 'necessary infrastructure to be "reasonably available" and "effective" vehicles for caller ID authentication trust under the TRACED Act.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating non‑IP proposals, the FCC should consider statutory tests of availability and effectiveness — i.e., whether infrastructure exists at scale and whether the solutions will reliably enable caller ID trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security, scalability, and cost‑effectiveness as evaluation metrics (USTelecom view)
rubrics_metrics.description: USTelecom pointed out that IP‑based solutions are more secure, scalable, and cost‑effective than any of the proposed non‑IP frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory assessment should weigh technical security properties, ability to scale across networks/providers, and comparative costs for deployment and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm deadline for providers to upgrade to IP (INCOMPAS/Cloud Communications Alliance recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: INCOMPAS and the Cloud Communications Alliance called for a firm deadline for providers to upgrade their networks to IP, arguing there is no technical or reasonable economic argument to prevent TDM‑in‑the‑middle providers from upgrading to IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fixed timetable is advocated to accelerate migration and reduce vulnerabilities caused by legacy interconnection points undermining STIR/SHAKEN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and mitigate legacy non‑IP interconnection undermining STIR/SHAKEN
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments noted that many providers' current implementation of STIR/SHAKEN is being undermined by legacy, non‑IP interconnection points (TDM‑in‑the‑middle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should address interoperability gaps and legacy interconnection that degrade end‑to‑end caller ID authentication effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑IP authentication adoption timeline and support for rural/smaller carriers (NTCA position)
rubrics_metrics.description: NTCA supports the FCC's proposals asserting non‑IP call authentication solutions are sufficiently available and effective, and recommended implementing a non‑IP solution within 18 to 24 months while adopting rules to ensure fair cost apportionment and regulatory support for rural carriers transitioning to IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators should consider phased timelines (e.g., 18–24 months), cost‑sharing or apportionment mechanisms, and targeted assistance to smaller/rural providers to avoid undue burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair cost apportionment and regulatory support for carriers transitioning to IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments urged rules to ensure fair cost apportionment and regulatory support for rural carriers that transition their networks to IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any mandate or timeline should be accompanied by mechanisms to distribute costs equitably (across carriers or via support programs) and provide transition assistance to smaller providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply comment period and procedural deadlines (administrative timeline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders will have another opportunity to weigh in during the reply comment period, which closes on August 15, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural schedule matters for participation: parties must file comments and reply comments by established deadlines to influence the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy goal of end‑to‑end IP‑based caller ID authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Several commenters emphasized the FCC's goal of end‑to‑end IP‑based call authentication (i.e., STIR/SHAKEN) as the preferred long‑term state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory strategy should be evaluated by how effectively it advances full end‑to‑end IP authentication across the network ecosystem rather than short‑term or partial fixes.
